web.markdown:
[Skip to main content](https://netlex.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/4414432672279-Configure-Subscription-Provider-ClickSign#main-content)

**ClickSign Account Registration:**

To configure the subscription provider you must have a platform Administrator profile.

Access the "Settings" menu in netLex:

![mceclip23.png](https://netlex.zendesk.com/hc/article_attachments/4414412480535)

Then click on "Standard Integrations":

![mceclip21.png](https://netlex.zendesk.com/hc/article_attachments/4414438077847)

Then click on "Add new provider":

![mceclip22.png](https://netlex.zendesk.com/hc/article_attachments/4414433838615)

Select the "ClickSign" provider and fill in the requested information:

![mceclip19.png](https://netlex.zendesk.com/hc/article_attachments/4414437980695)

Note: To configure this provider, it is necessary to exchange information between netlex and ClickSign.

How to get information and token from ClickSign:

1\. Go to https://app.clicksign.com

2\. On the Clicksign website access the "Settings in the side menu" area, as shown in the image below:

![mceclip11.png](https://netlex.zendesk.com/hc/article_attachments/4414412049815)![](https://netlex.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/Skip,%20since%20insertion%20is%20handled%20via%20gallery)![](https://netlex.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/Skip,%20since%20insertion%20is%20handled%20via%20gallery)

3\. In settings, navigate to the API tab

![mceclip18.png](https://netlex.zendesk.com/hc/article_attachments/4414412169111)

4\. Find the “Access token” section and click the “Generate access token” button

![mceclip12.png](https://netlex.zendesk.com/hc/article_attachments/4414427306903)

5\. Then define a name for the token and confirm to generate

![mceclip14.png](https://netlex.zendesk.com/hc/article_attachments/4414412080151)

6\. Once created, just copy the Access token code (shown in the image) to insert it into the netLex integration configuration

![mceclip15.png](https://netlex.zendesk.com/hc/article_attachments/4414433617687)

7\. Still on the API tab in Settings navigate to the Webhooks section and click the “Add Webhook” button

![mceclip13.png](https://netlex.zendesk.com/hc/article_attachments/4414412075543)

8\. Just enter the URL provided by netLex when creating the integration configuration and click on the button to create the webhook

![mceclip16.png](https://netlex.zendesk.com/hc/article_attachments/4414412137111)

9\. After adding the webhook the HMAC Secret code (indicated in the image) will be available, so just copy it and insert it in the field indicated in netLex to complete the configuration

![mceclip17.png](https://netlex.zendesk.com/hc/article_attachments/4414433660055)

## Unmaintained [Permalink: Unmaintained](https://github.com/NexoosBR/clicksign-api#unmaintained) The Clicksign-Api gem is **no longer maintained**. Please use the official [Clicksign Integration](https://www.clicksign.com/integracao/). ## Installation [Permalink: Installation](https://github.com/NexoosBR/clicksign-api#installation) Add this line to your application's Gemfile: ``` gem 'clicksign-api' ``` And then execute: ``` $ bundle ``` Or install it yourself as: ``` $ gem install clicksign-api ``` ## Setup: [Permalink: Setup:](https://github.com/NexoosBR/clicksign-api#setup) By default, all requests use Clicksign's SANDBOX. ``` credentials = { "key.production" => ENV["CLICKSIGN_ACCESS_TOKEN_PRODUCTION"] "key.sandbox" => ENV["CLICKSIGN_ACCESS_TOKEN_SANDBOX"] } Clicksign::API.configure do |config| config.credentials = credentials config.production = false end ``` To use PRODUCTION environment, you have to setup: ``` Clicksign::API.configure do |config| config.access_token = ENV['CLICKSIGN_ACCESS_TOKEN'] config.production = true end ``` ## Usage: [Permalink: Usage:](https://github.com/NexoosBR/clicksign-api#usage) To see all available parameters, please, check the [API docs](https://developers.clicksign.com/docs/informacoes-gerais). #### Create documents [Permalink: Create documents](https://github.com/NexoosBR/clicksign-api#create-documents) ``` file = File.open('/path/to/file/local/file.pdf', 'r') document = Clicksign::API::Document.create( params: { path: '/path/to/file/on/clicksign.pdf', file: file }, token: "key.sandbox") # => {"document"=> {"key"=>"00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"} ``` #### View documents [Permalink: View documents](https://github.com/NexoosBR/clicksign-api#view-documents) ``` find_document = Clicksign::API::Document.find(params: { key: response_document['document']['key'] }, token: "key.sandbox") # => {"document"=> {"key"=>"00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"} ``` #### Create Signers [Permalink: Create Signers](https://github.com/NexoosBR/clicksign-api#create-signers) ``` signer = Clicksign::API::Signer.create(params: { email: 'mail@email.com', auths: ['email'], delivery: 'email' }, token: "key.sandbox") # => {"signer"=> {"key"=>"00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"} ``` #### Add Signers to Document [Permalink: Add Signers to Document](https://github.com/NexoosBR/clicksign-api#add-signers-to-document) ``` signer_document = Clicksign::API::DocumentsSigners.create(params: { document_key: response_document['document']['key'], signer_key: response_signer['key'], sign_as: 'sign_as' }, token: "key.sandbox") # => {"list"=>{"key"=>"00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"} ``` ##### Creating Documents in Batches [Permalink: Creating Documents in Batches](https://github.com/NexoosBR/clicksign-api#creating-documents-in-batches) ``` batch = Clicksign::API::Batch.create( params: { document_keys: [response_document['document']['key'], 'other_document_key'], signer_key: response_signer['key'], summary: true }, token: "key.sandbox" ) # => {"batch"=>{"key"=>"00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"} ``` #### Notifying Signer by e-mail [Permalink: Notifying Signer by e-mail](https://github.com/NexoosBR/clicksign-api#notifying-signer-by-e-mail) ``` notify = Clicksign::API::Notifier.notify(params: { request_signature_key: 'request_signature_key' }, token: "key.sandbox") # => {:status=>202} ``` #### Notifying Signer by whatsapp [Permalink: Notifying Signer by whatsapp](https://github.com/NexoosBR/clicksign-api#notifying-signer-by-whatsapp) ``` notify = Clicksign::API::Notifier.notify(params: { request_signature_key: 'request_signature_key' }, token: "key.sandbox") # => {:status=>202} ## Development After checking out the repo, run `bin/setup` to install dependencies. Then, run `rake spec` to run the tests. You can also run `bin/console` for an interactive prompt that will allow you to experiment. To install this gem onto your local machine, run `bundle exec rake install`. To release a new version, update the version number in `version.rb`, and then run `bundle exec rake release`, which will create a git tag for the version, push git commits and tags, and push the `.gem` file to [rubygems.org](https://rubygems.org). ## Contributing Bug reports and pull requests are welcome on GitHub at https://github.com/[USERNAME]/clicksign-api. ``` ## About Clicksign's API ruby interface ### Topics [clicksign](https://github.com/topics/clicksign "Topic: clicksign") [clicksign-ruby](https://github.com/topics/clicksign-ruby "Topic: clicksign-ruby") [clicksign-api](https://github.com/topics/clicksign-api "Topic: clicksign-api") ### Resources [Readme](https://github.com/NexoosBR/clicksign-api#readme-ov-file) ### Uh oh! web.markdown:
[Portal Management and Administration](https://docs.clickhelp.com/articles/clickhelp-user-manual/documentation-portal-management)

# IP Allowlist

Updated on 4/29/20263 min read

Security policies often require that only users from a specific network should be able to access the portal, whereas connections for users belonging to other networks should be prohibited. A bright example is when the portal should only be accessible from office computers or via the office VPN server.

To handle this scenario, ClickHelp offers the **IP Allowlist**. It allows specifying a certain IP address or a range of IP addresses from which contributors can log in. This setting does not affect anonymous users and Power Readers.

ClickHelp accepts IPv4, IPv6 addresses, and ranges specified using the [CIDR notation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Classless_Inter-Domain_Routing).

This feature is available with the **Enterprise security** add-on for the **Growth** and **Professional** [pricing plans](https://clickhelp.com/online-documentation-tool-pricing/).


## Enable IP Allowlist [Link to this heading](https://docs.clickhelp.com/articles/clickhelp-user-manual/ip-allowlist/\#h2__2051240644 "Link to this heading")

To configure the IP allowlist:

1. Navigate to **Settings → Security → IP Allowlist**.

2. Select the **Allow specific IPs only** option.

3. Specify the desired IP address or a range of IP addresses in the text box below.

![Allow specific IPs only](https://docs.clickhelp.com/resources/Storage/clickhelp-user-manual/ip-allowlist/specific-ips.png)



|     |
| --- |
| To specify several IP addresses or ranges, put each record on a separate line. |

4. Select the [IP Allowlist mode](https://docs.clickhelp.com/articles/clickhelp-user-manual/ip-allowlist/#h2__758340511).
5. Save the changes.


That's it! Now, when a Contributor user whose IP address is different from the specified one or is outside of the specified range tries to log in or access any contributor-facing screen, they will get an error message saying they don't have permission to access the resource.

|     |
| --- |
| IP Allowlist is also applicable to API – when making an API call from a not-allowed IP address, the user will get a response with the 403 status code. |

## IP Allowlist Mode [Link to this heading](https://docs.clickhelp.com/articles/clickhelp-user-manual/ip-allowlist/\#h2__758340511 "Link to this heading")

The IP Allowlist mode determines the behavior when a client uses intermediary servers such as proxies, load balancers or CDNs to connect. In this case, the **X-Forwarded-For** (XFF) header is added to the requests. The XFF header includes a list of IP addresses: the original one and IP addresses of all intermediate servers that were passed. On the following screenshot you can see how the X-Forwarded-For header is formed:

![X-Forsarded-For header](https://docs.clickhelp.com/resources/Storage/clickhelp-user-manual/ip-allowlist/X-Forwarded-For-header.png)

You can select one of the following modes:

- **Validate all.** Checks both connection IP and all intermediate IP addresses that are specified in the X-Forwarded-For header. If at least one IP address is missed, the connection will be blocked. This mode is recommended for CDN usage and public proxy.

- **Trust proxy.** Check only connection IP. The information in the X-Forwarded-For header is ignored. This mode is recommended for trusted VPN or private proxy.


For direct portal access, only the connection IP is verified.

![](https://docs.clickhelp.com/resources/Storage/clickhelp-user-manual/%21Shared/icon-arrow-top.png)Back
